external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The content delivery network from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The server hosting the public site and running the CMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The CMS run by the web server.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database containing pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database
data_stores.notes: The source says: "I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk."

data_stores.name: CDN's bucket
data_stores.description: The bucket to which the web server publishes new assets.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: access site
data_flows.description: Readers access the public site through the web server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in

data_flows.name: fetch assets
data_flows.description: Readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: keep content
data_flows.description: The web server keeps pages, accounts and comments in the MySQL database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: publish assets
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says: "Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated".

data_flows.name: maintain database
data_flows.description: The admin maintains the database directly from wherever they happen to be.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database on the same hosted network.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site that readers access.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a public site whose readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database is confidential because it holds accounts and comments in addition to pages.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains pages, accounts and comments.

assumptions.assumption: The CMS is confidential because it reads, writes or transforms account and comment data held by the database.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web server runs the CMS and keeps accounts and comments in the database.

assumptions.assumption: The web server handles personal data because it keeps accounts and comments in the database.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web server keeps accounts and comments.

assumptions.assumption: The web-server-to-database flow carries personal data because it keeps accounts and comments.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the web server keeps accounts and comments in the MySQL database.

assumptions.assumption: The admin-to-database flow carries personal data because the database contains accounts and comments.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the database as containing accounts and comments.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN bucket holds public data because it contains assets that are published and fetched by readers.
assumptions.basis: The source says assets are published to the CDN's bucket and readers fetch them from the CDN.
